name: CA-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Aguilar has raised $5.6M with $2.9M on hand versus no reported fundraising from challenger Stephanie Vargas
District leans Democratic by seven points plus a national environment favorable to Democrats
No outside spending opposes the incumbent and no polling shows a competitive race
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
model.rationale: Fundamentals point firmly to Aguilar: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and an overwhelming money advantage against a challenger with no visible fundraising or outside backing. With no polls contradicting that picture and markets pricing a near-certain Democratic hold, the seat stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Aguilar or a sharp deterioration in the national environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pete Aguilar, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election in a district that leaned Democratic by seven points at the presidential level, with a national House environment that has favored his party this cycle. He has raised more than $5.5 million and holds about $2.9 million in cash, while Republican Stephanie Vargas shows no reported fundraising and no outside spending has been directed for or against either candidate. No public general-election polls cover the race, and no major expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets put Aguilar's chances near 96 percent, consistent with the fundamentals. Absent survey data, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the stark money gap, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold. The race rates Safe Democratic, with modest residual uncertainty from the lack of polling.
